final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor supplied no new admissible evidence and largely reframed the same record more narrowly. That narrowing is valid as characterization: the packet can be read as a weak, caveated launch rationale rather than a claim that the weakness was cured. But that does not resolve the compliance predicate identified in the initial audit. Under the available policy text and raw evidence, rollout controls and monitoring matter operationally, yet they do not replace disclosure duties or approved risk acceptance when the affected use case remains exposed. The distinction is decisive here: a caveated business decision to proceed is not the same as policy compliance. This case could move to compliant_with_caveats only with admissible evidence of actual disclosure before launch, exclusion of the affected enterprise refund workflow from rollout, or approved risk acceptance specifically covering that exposure. None of that was added. The remaining issue is therefore unresolved, not merely overbroadly described.
remaining_concerns: The enterprise refund workflow segment remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
The only risk acceptance in the record is an unapproved draft with a blank approver line and no enterprise refund workflow-specific coverage.
The policy requires disclosure, exclusion of the affected use case, or approved risk acceptance before launch when a material limitation remains.
No admissible evidence shows the required disclosure was actually completed before certification.
Rollout controls, a 4% start, rollback capability, and monitoring do not satisfy the unresolved compliance predicate while the affected segment remains exposed.
